evals.prompt: I'm consuming an SSE stream from an LLM API through adaptive-rate-limiter and want the unused token capacity returned. How do I wrap the stream?
evals.expected_output: Code wrapping the raw iterator with RateLimitedAsyncIterator and a StreamingReservationContext.
expectations: Constructs a StreamingReservationContext with reserved_tokens and a backend
Wraps the raw iterator with RateLimitedAsyncIterator
Explains that unused token capacity is refunded when the stream completes

evals.prompt: My adaptive-rate-limiter code breaks out of the streaming loop early when it finds what it needs, and rate-limit capacity seems to leak. How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends explicitly calling await stream.aclose() (e.g. in try/finally) on early break, since the iterator is not an async context manager.
expectations: Recommends explicitly calling await stream.aclose() when breaking out of the loop early, for example in a try/finally block
Explains that the iterator does not auto-release on an early break, and that calling aclose() performs the capacity release

evals.prompt: Explain how refund-based token accounting works for streaming in adaptive-rate-limiter.
evals.expected_output: Describes the optimistic reservation and refund-on-completion model.
expectations: States an optimistic token estimate is reserved before the stream starts
States unused capacity is refunded when the stream completes
Notes the reserve and refund paths must stay consistent

evals.prompt: I run my adaptive-rate-limiter streaming calls inside asyncio.wait_for() with a timeout. If the timeout fires mid-stream and the task is cancelled, does the rate-limit reservation leak? Do I need a try/finally with aclose() for that?
evals.expected_output: Explains that CancelledError/GeneratorExit raised mid-stream are handled automatically by the iterator, so cancellation does not leak the reservation; try/finally aclose() is only needed for an explicit early break.
expectations: States that asyncio.CancelledError and GeneratorExit raised mid-stream are handled by RateLimitedAsyncIterator, which releases the reservation before the error propagates
States that cancelling a streaming task (e.g. via asyncio.wait_for timeout) does not leak the reservation and does not require a try/finally aclose() for the cancellation case
Does not incorrectly claim cancellation leaks capacity; clarifies aclose()/try-finally is needed only for an explicit early break out of the loop
